title: Factors Considered in Deciding Deportation Destinations for Foreigners Who Have Served Their Sentences in Singapore
what_it_is: Factors Considered in Deciding Deportation Destinations for Foreigners Who Have Served Their Sentences in Singapore

sections.label: Deportation country considerations for foreigners
sections.summary: Question asks what considerations decide which country foreigners convicted in Singapore are deported to, and how they apply to the money laundering case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) for foreigners convicted of offences in Singapore, what are the considerations taken into account in deciding which country to deport them to after they have served their sentences; and (b) how are these considerations applied to the offenders involved in the recent billion-dollar money laundering case.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This applies similarly to the convicted foreigners in the $3 billion money laundering case.

sections.label: Foreigners' allowed destination countries
sections.summary: Foreigners can go to any country their passport or travel document allows them to go to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I alluded to in my main reply, the foreigners can go to any country to which their passport or travel document allows them to go.

sections.label: Deportations to Cambodia and Japan
sections.summary: Convicted foreigners can go to any country their passports allow; seven convicts were deported to Cambodia and one to Japan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For the avoidance of doubt, to be clear, convicted foreigners can go to any country which their passports or travel documents allow them to go.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, for the subjects that we are discussing right now, seven convicts have been deported to Cambodia, while one convict has been deported to Japan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Specifically, on the question on three of the subjects as to whether or not they hold Cambodian passports, I can check back with my Ministry on this point.

sections.label: Admissibility assessment for deportation
sections.summary: The Cambodia-China extradition treaty was not part of decision-making; assessment covers passports held and greatest likelihood of admissibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To answer the second question first, whether or not there was an extradition treaty between Cambodia and China was not part of the decision-making process that the Ministry undertook.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, I think we do not want a situation where we try to deport an individual and actually the country to which we are deporting the individual to, does not accept the individual.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Therefore, I think there is an assessment: firstly, based on the passports that they hold, which are the countries they can be deported to; secondly, obviously, if they have multiple passports, we would have to, well, whether or not the term is "choose", but we would have to decide which country that they have the greatest likelihood of being admissible to.

sections.label: Offender's preference and Ministry assessment
sections.summary: An offender can indicate a preferred country, but the Ministry assesses whether the individual is admissible based on their travel document.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Can the offender choose where to be deported to and the Government will accede to the choice?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I think you are using the term "choice" rather loosely, because the offender can indicate which country he or she would like to be deported to, but it cannot just be, "I choose and therefore I will be sent there".

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: There needs to be an assessment by the Ministry as to whether or not the individual can be admissible to the country based on the travel document that he or she holds.
